newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Capel B&K keeps India Sterlite hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Capel B&K keeps India Sterlite hold.

text.p: Securities firm James Capel B&K said it kept its "hold" recommendation on Indian cable firm Sterlite Industries even though the firm would benefit from the waiver of a minimum tax requirement on backward units.

Capel B&K analyst Sonal Jhaveri said a telecom scandal -- involving several top officials of India's Department of Telecommunications (DoT) -- was taking its toll with the cancellation of optic fibre cable (OFC) tenders.

"Since the DoT is hard pressed for meeting its targets in the current year, having slipped in 1995/96 (April-March), we envisage only a delay in fresh orders during 1996/97," Jhaveri said in a note to investors.
She downgraded sales estimates for the OFC division by a third, saying it would affect 1996/97 earnings by 5.7 percent.

Jhaveri said Sterlite's jelly filled telephone cables plant was located at Silvassa, a notified backward area, allowing it tax exemption for the first five years from January 1994 and a 30 percent concessional rate for an additional five years.
"The copper rod plant, which started production in January 1996, also has the same benefits," Jhaveri said.
She said after exemption from the 12.9 percent minimum alternate tax (MAT) for firms in backward areas, the company would have to pay tax only on OFC sales.
"The overall impact on earnings is +7.8 percent thanks to tax savings," Jhaveri said.
"We continue our Hold recommendation with this additional uncertainty on OFC orders, since commerical production of the copper smelter seems months away," Jhaveri added.
Sterlite has plans to build a greenfield copper smelter in the western Indian state of Maharashtra.
